### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://h178.com/iine_comments](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fh178.com%2Fiine_comments) ### Comment > The site's anti-adblock is triggered when the **Base filter** is enabled. > This issue can **only be reproduced on iOS** (Safari). > And I could not reproduce it on desktop(chrome) with the same filter set. > > ## Reproduction Results > > | Filters enabled | Result | > |---|---| > | Base + Japanese | Anti-adblock **IS shown** (NG) | > | Japanese only | Normal (OK) | > | Base only | Anti-adblock **IS shown** (NG) | > > ## Analysis > > The issue occurs with the Base filter alone, and it **persists even when the Japanese filter is enabled alongside it**. In other words, the Japanese filter is currently unable to fully counteract the problem caused by the Base filter. I see two possible explanations: > > **1. The Japanese filter lacks a proper exception / countermeasure** > > The Japanese filter may simply not contain an exception (or an anti-adblock circumvention rule) that overrides the problematic rule in the Base filter. If so, we first need to identify **which rule in the Base filter** triggers the site's anti-adblock detection. > > **2. The countermeasure exists, but it is too slow on iOS (timing issue)** > > Since the problem is reproducible **only on iOS**, it may not be a matter of a "missing rule" at all. On iOS, advanced rules are applied by the Safari extension rather than by the content blocker, so they can be injected **later than the page's own anti-adblock check runs**. If the Japanese filter relies on a scriptlet to hide or neutralize the detection, it might simply lose the race on iOS while working fine on desktop. > > > ## Steps Already Tried (none resolved the issue) > > - Updated the filter rules to the latest version > - Updated the AdGuard iOS app to the latest version > - Restarted the device > - Cleared Safari's cache > - Disabled all content blockers in Safari settings and enabled them again > - Restarted Safari > - Restarted AdGuard > - Checked for filter updates in AdGuard (wait 1 min) > > Reinstalling AdGuard is unlikely to change this behavior, as a clean filter update and a full app/device restart have already been performed. > > ## Additional Information > > - The only Safari extension enabled is AdGuard, so interference from other extensions can be ruled out. > - This issue may be related to: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/237902#issuecomment-5253021366 ### Screenshots
